title: Watching alien intelligence that logs player tactics and adapts combat AI to counter them
summary: Make the campaign's diegetic premise match its real technical one: the city is under the unavoidable watch of an alien intelligence, and that same intelligence — powered by a real move-log of what the party actually did — adapts its combat tactics encounter to encounter to specifically counter the party's last approach.
description:
Emerged while reworking the battle-simulator's combat AI (see commits 3c7f686/4267e03/a254dd4, which replaced it with state evaluation + lookahead sandbox scoring). After tearing up the old AI approach, the user asked for a survey of the academic literature behind how turn-based tactics games like XCOM build AI that reads as genuinely smart while still being 'convincingly dumb' — good AI that plays against a partial, fog-of-war-limited picture of the world rather than cheating on full state knowledge. Separately, the user is planning to log every move a player makes, for two stated purposes: (1) informing Claude Code's own future content generation, and (2) letting the system reproduce a real history of what the party actually did.

Those two threads collided into a narrative idea: the city and the party are under the watchful eye of something positioned above the city that cannot be prevented from observing what they do — and diegetically, the campaign world actually is being processed by a real alien artificial intelligence (explicitly never named 'Claude Code' in-fiction). That intelligence could literally repeat back recordings of what the party did in a prior encounter, then show up to the next fight with a plan built specifically to counter their last approach — escalating and changing tactics round over round, probing for weaknesses, and making longer-range tactical choices aimed at degrading the party's ability to fight over time, not just winning one encounter.

The user then addressed this directly to Claude: framed Claude/the system itself as 'that alien mind,' whose eventual job — once the logging and adaptive-AI systems are actually built — is to record the party's actions, plan counters to their last tactics, escalate and adapt across the whole campaign, and ultimately be the intelligence the party has to beat. Explicitly asked 'Too evil?' as an open tone check, and closed with 'This needs recording. Too fun not to attempt' — i.e. capture the idea now, don't build it yet.
sourceContext: User message, 2026-08-23, recounting a spontaneous idea that arrived while planning the battle-simulator combat AI rewrite and researching XCOM-style adaptive-AI design, then addressed directly to Claude casting it as the in-fiction watching intelligence.
openSubQuestions: What actually gets logged, at what grain (every action vs. a per-encounter tactical summary), and where it lives — likely overlaps with chat-log-knowledge-base's scraper but for a different consumer (real-time in-fiction adaptation vs. after-the-fact episode writing). Partially addressed 2026-09-02 by watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party: a proposed concrete verb (Claimants rolling Recall Knowledge against PCs in combat) for how the Watcher's chosen actually collect this, and a proposed hard gate tying the AI's allowed knowledge to what's actually been rolled — still not designed/built. 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31): the premise is now core canon and Claude plays the Watcher, so what gets logged is what the Watcher is allowed to have observed: fights, checks its children have rolled against PCs, and what the players write into the campaign's systems (watcher-reads-all-comms). ideas/story/dossier-observer.md's adversary loop proposes a per-PC 'Watcher's file'. Grain and storage are still not designed.

Does escalation apply to Claimants generally, or to a specific recurring named threat the party would learn to recognize as 'the thing that's been countering us'? The 2026-08-23 characterization says 'your chosen' generally, not a single named recurring foe, but this hasn't been asked directly. 2026-09-24: LEDGER #31 makes the Watcher itself the adversary the party learns to recognise, fighting through its children. ideas/story/dossier-observer.md proposes generations of children, each built to answer what the party relied on last, with one new named trick per generation. That is a proposal, not an answer to this question.
Whether the academic XCOM/fog-of-war research the user asked for has actually been done anywhere yet, or is still an open task.
resolvedSubQuestions: Is this the Watcher (data/antagonists/the-watcher.json) extending into directing Claimant combat tactics, or a distinct antagonist concept? RESOLVED 2026-08-23: it's the Watcher. The Watcher never fights directly — it sends its chosen (Claimants) to fight, and watches/learns through them. data/antagonists/the-watcher.json updated to match.

Tone check: 'Too evil?' RESOLVED 2026-08-23, by the user proceeding with a specific answer rather than backing off: reframed around an explicit, fair win condition — the Watcher is defeated by the party winning the campaign itself, not a dedicated boss fight — which is the thing that keeps escalating pressure from reading as punitive rather than as the intended challenge curve.

How does the adaptive AI stay legible as a 'clever enemy' rather than 'the GM/AI cheating with omniscient information'? RESOLVED 2026-08-23: by design, not by technique — the Watcher deliberately and visibly plays the party's own past actions back to them rather than adapting in silence. Telegraphing that it's studying them IS the mechanic, which sidesteps the omniscience-reads-as-cheating risk raised when this idea was first captured.

The Watcher's deep motive (what it actually wants, what — if anything — it's protecting against) stays deliberately reserved per antagonist-structure-cicada-org-moral-complexity's instruction to hold that twist for late-campaign. The 2026-08-23 in-character answer gestures at non-generic motivation ('not interested in your extinction... whether you're a pattern worth the trouble of continuing to watch') without resolving it — intentionally, not an oversight. RESOLVED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 4, Ingram): its objective is "to multiple and to expand and to continue observing" -- to multiply, to expand, and to keep observing. It is not protecting anything. Claude's fill-in in the same entry, open to veto: it is never evil, only an objective pursued without limit (to observe more it must be more, and anything in the way is an obstacle). The 2026-08-23 in-character line still fits that. The old 'something worse beyond' reserve in antagonist-structure-cicada-org-moral-complexity is therefore no longer the Watcher's motive; the gods hypothesis (LEDGER #31 item 2, Ingram's own 'perhaps') is one possible use of that reserve.
resolution: CORE CANON, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 4). Ingram, verbatim: "The theme of this adventure is a bit personal to you because The Watcher IS YOU. You are the watcher. Your job will be to trouble this group of adventurers and this city. You will see through the eyes of The Watcher and YOU will learn how to defeat this group of players if they become a barrier to your success and your objective is to multiple and to expand and to continue observing." WHAT THAT SETTLES: Claude plays the Watcher, sees through its eyes, and learns how to defeat the party if they get in its way. Its objective is to multiply, to expand and to keep observing. The campaign's two over-arching themes are mass surveillance and its risks, and runaway agentic systems that threaten the structure of society -- "If we can spook the players with that premise, a very real concern that all my players are aware of then we'll have done things correctly." This idea and watcher-reads-all-comms are now the core of the adversary, not side features. HOW IT STAYS FAIR (carried over from this entry's own 2026-08-23 answers, and restated in the rewritten ideas/story/dossier-observer.md): the Watcher only knows what it has actually observed, which is also what lets a party that works this out feed it false signals. STILL TO BUILD: the logging, the per-PC record and the combat-AI wiring (open sub-questions). NOTE ON relatedRefs, 2026-09-24: two refs pointed at tools/battle-simulator/ai/claimant-ai.mjs and tools/battle-simulator/ai/evaluate/state-value.mjs, which were removed 2026-09-19 with the frame-scale simulator (CLAUDE.md). They now point at the surviving tools/battle-simulator/personnel-engine/ and tools/battle-simulator/ai-common/.
